rewrites.title: Lineage tracking of transmission across divisions
rewrites.description: Track lineages with live reporters or barcoded clones to measure whether the primed state persists through cell divisions and decays at a defined rate. Perturb candidate carriers (BAF/SWI-SNF recruitment, pioneer cofactors, histone marks, mitotic bookmarking of AP-1) to identify which mechanism transmits the memory, and fit a quantitative model to heritability versus decay.

rewrites.title: Mutual information between stimulus history and AP-1 state
rewrites.description: Deliver defined stimulus sequences differing in order, dose, and spacing (A-then-B versus B-then-A, pulsed versus sustained). Compute the mutual information between stimulus history and single-cell AP-1 occupancy/accessibility, and compare it with the same measure for the rest of the transcriptome. This determines how much information about past stimulation AP-1 carries and whether it encodes order and magnitude or only prior exposure versus none.

rewrites.title: Mitotic retention and sublineage re-induction timing
rewrites.description: Use live imaging of HaloTag-tagged JunB or Fos and mitotic ChIP-seq to measure whether AP-1 remains bound to mitotic chromosomes. Sort daughter-cell sublineages from a barcoded or photoconvertible lineage and measure whether re-induction latency is inherited through division, testing heritability of the memory state rather than its maintenance in interphase.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN after a transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or epidermal stem cells) to a transient stimulus such as injury, TPA, or cytokines. Profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding from hours to weeks after the stimulus is withdrawn. Persistent AP-1-motif-associated accessibility or persistent AP-1 occupancy would indicate a memory-like state.

rewrites.title: Inducible, time-resolved AP-1 perturbation with chromatin readout
rewrites.description: Use an acute, reversible degron (e.g., dTAG or AID) or optogenetic control to deplete or activate FOS/JUN for defined windows. Then track whether chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac, and AP-1 motif occupancy at enhancers persist after the stimulus is withdrawn. Persistence without AP-1 present would be direct evidence of memory, while rapid collapse would argue against it.

rewrites.title: Protein turnover versus chromatin residence
rewrites.description: Use Halo or SNAP tags on Fos or Jun to measure protein half-life and chromatin dwell time by pulse-chase. If the chromatin mark outlasts the protein, memory must be carried by something other than the AP-1 protein, such as a self-sustaining chromatin state.

rewrites.title: Locus-specific AP-1 motif perturbation and artificial memory writing
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR editing of AP-1 motifs, or dCas9-based recruitment or blocking of AP-1 or chromatin remodelers (e.g., SWI/SNF) at candidate enhancers, together with optogenetic or pulsed AP-1 activation. Determine whether motif loss erases memory and whether a synthetic pulse is sufficient to induce a persistent primed state, testing necessity and sufficiency.

rewrites.title: Acute degron removal after the stimulus
rewrites.description: Prime cells, then deplete AP-1 with a dTAG or auxin degron (e.g., c-JUN, or a dominant-negative A-FOS) only after the stimulus has cleared. Measure whether the faster secondary response and open chromatin persist. If memory survives AP-1 loss, it is held in chromatin rather than in AP-1, distinguishing AP-1 as memory carrier from AP-1 as initiator of the chromatin change.

rewrites.title: Allele-specific memory in F1 hybrid or heterozygous-donor cells
rewrites.description: In F1 hybrid mouse cells or human donor cells heterozygous at thousands of AP-1 motifs, perform allele-resolved ATAC and nascent RNA before and long after a transient stimulus. Test whether the persistent (memory) state tracks the motif-disrupting allele in cis. The many natural motif variants provide a genome-scale, internally controlled causal test, and motifs showing memory loss without loss of acute induction identify those needed specifically for maintenance.

rewrites.title: Epigenome-editing dissociation experiment
rewrites.description: Target dCas9-KRAB or dCas9-p300 to AP-1 motifs to erase or write chromatin marks without changing AP-1 binding. If the memory follows the edited chromatin state rather than the presence of the transcription factor, the chromatin state, not the factor, carries the memory.

rewrites.title: Drosophila wing disc regeneration: JNK/AP-1 chromatin memory
rewrites.description: After transient ablation (e.g., eiger or rpr pulse) in Drosophila wing imaginal discs, profile Fos/Jun (Kayak/Jra) binding and chromatin accessibility (CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq) in regenerated versus never-damaged tissue at multiple time points after healing. Then re-injure and test whether the primed enhancers show faster or stronger transcriptional and regenerative responses, and whether acute Fos/Jun knockdown (TARGET/Gal80ts) during the initial injury alone abolishes this priming.

rewrites.title: Degron depletion of AP-1 between priming and rechallenge
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on endogenous FOS, JUN, JUNB and FOSL1 to eliminate AP-1 selectively during the interval between a priming stimulus and a rechallenge, leaving the induction and readout phases intact. If priming survives AP-1 loss during this interval, AP-1 establishes the memory in chromatin; if priming collapses, persistence of AP-1 protein is itself the memory. The two cases are distinguished by the timing of depletion.

rewrites.title: Live single-cell reporter tracking across divisions
rewrites.description: Express a destabilized fluorescent reporter driven by an AP-1-responsive promoter and track individual cells by time-lapse microscopy through priming, rest, and re-stimulation. Compare the fraction of cells that retain the primed state and whether daughter cells inherit it, to determine whether memory is confined to a subpopulation and whether it is heritable.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis of AP-1 activity versus stimulus dose
rewrites.description: Ramp stimulus intensity up and then back down in single-cell time series (e.g., Fos or c-Jun reporter intensity against stimulus level) and compare the rising and falling limbs. A loop that persists, with nonzero enclosed area, means AP-1 output depends on stimulation history rather than on the current dose alone.

rewrites.title: Memory decay timescale via re-stimulation after variable rest
rewrites.description: Give a priming pulse, wait for varied intervals (minutes to weeks, spanning cell divisions), then give a second test pulse and measure changes in response amplitude and kinetics. Fit the decay of the primed-versus-naive response difference to obtain the memory timescale, and compare it with AP-1 level, binding, and chromatin marks to test whether AP-1 is required for persistence.

rewrites.title: Heritability of AP-1 state across clonal lineages
rewrites.description: Use live-cell reporters of AP-1 activity (e.g., TRE-driven fluorescent protein) with long-term imaging and cell tracking to quantify mother-daughter and sister-sister correlations in reporter level. Fit the decay of correlation with generation number to estimate a memory half-life. Pair this with single-cell RNA/ATAC profiling of sorted high- and low-reporter cells to confirm that the imaging readout reflects a broader transcriptional state.

rewrites.title: Replication-coupled dilution and re-establishment kinetics
rewrites.description: Pulse-label nascent chromatin (EdU/BrdU capture or nascent-chromatin ATAC) at defined times after a stimulus to measure how much AP-1 occupancy and accessibility survive passage of the replication fork, how fast they are restored on daughter strands, and whether sister chromatids inherit them symmetrically. Self-propagating memory should show rapid template-directed restoration rather than slow re-equilibration from bulk AP-1 levels.

rewrites.title: Persistence of AP-1 motif accessibility after stimulus washout
rewrites.description: Track AP-1 motif accessibility and occupancy in single cells with paired ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag over days after stimulus removal, separating chromatin states that persist from transcription that has returned to baseline. This could be done in primary neurons or T cells, with the key readout being whether accessibility outlasts AP-1 binding.

rewrites.title: Heritability through mitosis with lineage tracing
rewrites.description: Sort or live-image primed cells and follow daughter cells across several divisions using an AP-1 reporter and a target-gene reporter. Add mitotic-bookmarking assays such as CUT&Tag on mitotically arrested cells. Quantify how memory decays over divisions and whether AP-1 bookmarking predicts which lineages retain memory.

rewrites.title: Degron-based maintenance test after stimulus washout
rewrites.description: Use an auxin-inducible degron on endogenous c-Fos or JUNB, stimulate, wash out, and degrade AP-1 at different times after the pulse. Track enhancer accessibility (ATAC-seq) and target transcription to determine whether persistence requires continued AP-1 presence, and compare with histone-mark readouts (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) to separate AP-1-dependent maintenance from chromatin-encoded memory.
